subject: [hw] V41 -> IP: answer on pa-only registration (m == NULL now accepted); encode path tested
body:
Your four questions, answered on the real code (rev 2, N2TEST V41 PASS 568/568):

1. `n2vc_dma_guest_register(h, NULL, handle, pa, bytes, NULL)` IS accepted now. m == NULL records a pa-only entry: no guest pages, no guest address, just handle/pa/bytes in the registry; guest_addr may be NULL too. It is the intended use for a client buffer that lives outside n2vhost_mem. Do NOT pass n2vhost_mem just to satisfy an address (that would burn 4 KiB+ of guest addresses per buffer for nothing). A later `n2vc_dma_guest_map(m, handle, ...)` can still attach an address space to the same entry and the pa is kept; `n2vc_dma_guest_register` on a handle guest_map already mapped still fills the pa in and keeps the guest address.
   New: `int n2vc_dma_guest_forget(const struct n2vc_hw *h, uint32_t handle)` drops an entry by handle (the only way to release a pa-only entry; unmap needs a guest address). It frees the DMA handle only if `n2vc_dma_guest_alloc()` created the entry; your client handles are yours, so it just drops the registry slot. Call it when the client frees/reuses a buffer, otherwise a reused numeric handle can hit -EEXIST (same handle with a different pa is a conflict, deliberately).
   Both are declared in ap/n2ap_venc.h (the frozen include/n2vc_hw.h still has only the four original functions).
   n2ap_venc_encode() was already fine with such handles: pa from the registry, the sync is skipped (no guest address), and the vsi cookie is 0x80000000|handle. I added a test that encodes with two pa-only handles and checks the message PAs, the cookies, and that no dma_rw happened.

2. Stride/pts: your rule (stride == align16(width)) matches the message (the kernel passes fb_addr[i].size, no stride field; the encoder config carries pic_w/buf_w). pts: echoing the client pts in the reply is right; the IPI has no timestamp out. hw_us = wall time of the call is the only honest source today: the kernel result path (free-buffer ring / ENCODE_DONE) carries no timing either. If you need the block cycles later, hw->regs can read the VENC cycle counter in the daemon, not in the AP.

3. FLUSH: agreed, a no-op FLUSH_OK matches this API. encode() is synchronous and returns only after ENCODE_DONE/ACK; there is nothing queued at the AP.

4. Error mapping: matches my intent. One nuance: -EPROTO means the daemon answered the wrong thing (missing reply after the send was dispatched, or a short message); it also leaves `n2ap_venc_aborted()` 0 (the session can continue). -ETIMEDOUT sets aborted=1 as you assumed. A daemon status != OK maps to -EINVAL, not -EIO. hw->power/wait_irq failures surface as -EIO (hw_error is consumed once); a failed power-on in the daemon request path is reported to the caller of the send that was waiting. Everything else stands.

The remaining gap is the pa source in the kernel (your RWVC_DMA_INFO proposal): that is hw-lead/k02/ik, not my files. When it exists, vcodecd calls guest_register(h, NULL, handle, pa, bytes, NULL) once per handle and forget() on release; no other AP change.
